audit_findings.title: Forward interest expense may be understated as low-coupon debt refinances
audit_findings.magnitude: 1H 2026 net interest expense increased $14 million year over year and external-debt interest increased $13 million; replacing the $681 million-equivalent 0.318% notes principally with $700 million of 4.488% notes implies approximately $29 million of additional annual gross coupon expense; full-ladder effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Raises recurring interest expense retained in equity-level OE, reducing forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: A portion of the proceeds from the September 2025 issuance of $500 million notes listed above will be used to fund the repayment at maturity of the Company's currently outstanding ¥21.5 billion Japanese Yen denominated 0.370% notes due March 18, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The upward refinancing reset is demonstrated, although the cited yen notes were repaid with cash rather than replaced one-for-one. The 2025 anchor contains only partial-year expense from the September 2025 issuance and none of the May 2026 issuance. The immediate reset is about 2% of anchor OE before tax, and additional low-coupon maturities across the $8.436 billion June 2026 debt balance make the cumulative valuation effect reasonably capable of being material.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild annual interest expense through every debt maturity using contractual coupons, actual 2026 issuances and repayments, plausible replacement-rate scenarios, debt-issuance-cost amortization, and separately purged interest income; rerun all scenarios from adjusted after-tax OE.

audit_findings.title: Parent-attributable earnings may be mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated D&A and cash addbacks can overstate parent OE and the bridge, while consolidated maintenance-capex deductions can understate parent OE; NCI claims also sit ahead of parent common shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Results of these entities are consolidated with our financial and operational results.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter inconsistency if parent-attributable net income was combined with unallocated consolidated adjustments. The record does not identify the NCI share of each adjustment. At June 2026, ordinary NCI was $188 million and redeemable NCI was $106 million, while 1H 2026 NCI earnings were $34 million; these show a real minority claim but do not establish the valuation misstatement because the direction and ownership allocation of the OE adjustments remain unknown.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile D&A, amortization, maintenance capex, cash and short-term investments entity by entity to the parent's ownership percentage; identify the redemption value and terms of the $106 million redeemable NCI, then rerun OE and the bridge using only parent-owned amounts.

audit_findings.title: Uncapped separation indemnities could create an unmodeled senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Any obligation not already expensed or accrued reduces future OE when paid or requires a separate deduction from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Indemnities that we may be required to provide RTX and/or Carrier are not subject to any cap, may be significant and could negatively impact our business.
audit_findings.explanation: The uncapped contractual exposure and an active RTX dispute are demonstrated, but no filed loss range establishes the incremental claim. The latest filing carries a $55 million RTX indemnity payable and reports $63 million of separation-related payments in 1H 2026; those recorded amounts must not be charged twice. The possibility of additional obligations is current rather than merely forward-looking, but its materiality cannot be determined from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the TMA and other separation agreements, dispute submissions, counsel's probability-weighted exposure range, post-June accrual changes and payment schedule; deduct only amounts not already reflected in OE or the $55 million payable.

audit_findings.title: The gross cash addback may include customer advances and required operating liquidity
audit_findings.magnitude: $871 million bridge addback at risk, equal to $2.24 per diluted share and 4.0% of the $22.009 billion base equity value; exact excess-cash haircut unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Overstates the equity bridge by treating all cash and short-term investments as distributable surplus while OE excludes working-capital movements.
audit_findings.evidence: Contract liabilities relate to payments received in advance of the satisfaction of performance under the contract.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds the entire $871 million of cash and short-term investments without establishing that it is excess. June 2026 contract liabilities were $3.049 billion, net contract liabilities were $2.225 billion, supplier-finance obligations were $716 million, 73% of cash was held abroad and restricted cash was separately $36 million. These liabilities do not mechanically offset cash dollar for dollar, but they establish operating and performance claims large enough that the full addback cannot be presumed distributable. The bridge exposure is large enough to affect per-share value materially.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a June 2026 legal-entity liquidity schedule covering customer advances, supplier-finance balances, restricted or trapped cash, repatriation taxes, near-term debt and operating requirements; replace the gross addback with verified distributable excess cash and rerun per-share values.

audit_findings.title: The pension deficit may not be fully represented by accounting pension expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $284 million FY2025 underfunded position, equal to $0.73 per diluted share and 1.3% of base equity value; expected 2026 contributions are $45 million versus $36 million of 2025 pension cost
audit_findings.mechanism: Any deficit funding above pension expense retained in OE would reduce future OE or require a separate bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to make total contributions of approximately $ 45 million to our global defined benefit pension plans in 2026, including benefit payments to be paid directly from corporate assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The deficit is real, but its filed scale is modest relative to the $22.009 billion base equity value and cannot change the present conclusion that even the $66.46 bull value is below the $71.21 market price. Near-term cash requirements also do not show a large omitted burden: expected 2026 contributions exceed 2025 pension cost by only $9 million, and 1H 2026 contributions of $21 million were close to $20 million of periodic benefit cost. Deducting the entire deficit would itself be conservative because accounting pension expense already captures part of the obligation.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the OE calculation retained the $36 million pension cost and compare actuarial contribution forecasts with normalized expense; recognize only the present value of incremental funding not already captured in OE.

audit_findings.title: Recurring service-portfolio purchases may be missing from maintenance investment
audit_findings.magnitude: filed acquisition and intangible-asset spending of $36 million in 2023, $87 million in 2024, $109 million in 2025 and $193 million in 1H 2026; required maintenance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back purchased-portfolio amortization without deducting recurring portfolio-replacement spending overstates OE; acquisition-dependent growth also makes the modeled growth rates require additional reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: Our acquisitions of businesses and intangible assets, net of cash, totaled $ 109 million, $ 87 million and $ 36 million (including debt assumed) in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively, and were primarily in our Service segment.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring cash spending and purchased-service-portfolio amortization are demonstrated, while the portion needed merely to maintain the portfolio is unresolved. FY2025 spending was 7.7% of the $1.424 billion OE anchor, and the 2026 pace increased substantially, although $170 million related to a specific French acquisition. Because service produces 91% of FY2025 segment operating profit and forecast value assumes continuing service growth, even a fraction of this spending treated as maintenance could materially reduce OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $62 million FY2025 intangible amortization included in the OE addback, separate organic service growth from acquired growth, quantify portfolio attrition and replacement cost, classify each acquisition as maintenance or expansion, and rerun scenarios after deducting normalized maintenance acquisition spending.
